title: The diagonal Roos comparison of an exact equivalence
statement: For abelian categories A and B with countable products and an additive functor F:A→B, the canonical Roos map has the first and second coordinate formulas given by the product comparison, and is natural in every strict tower. If F is an equivalence, this map is an isomorphism, on arbitrary unbounded towers. [def-pod-completion-reindex-models]

source.place: Steps 1 and 5; strict quotient and Roos comparison argument.

proof.text:
use scalarRoosMap, which is uniquely specified by both cocone coordinates
and every product projection. Its degree-i coordinate matrix is the direct sum
of the product comparisons in degrees i and i-1. Those comparisons are invertible
because an equivalence preserves products. The additive functor preserves the
biproduct decomposition of the source cocone, so the displayed matrix proves
invertibility in every degree. A chain map invertible in every degree is an
isomorphism of complexes. No acyclicity, boundedness, or completeness is needed.
